product: Mortgage
consumer_complaint_narrative:
At the end of XX/XX/XXXX, we were notified that our Mortgage was assigned to Mr. Cooper, the new Mortgagor. In our notice of assignment, we were guaranteed a smooth transition and were told that we did not need to do anything to facilitate the assignment/transition. The mortgage was transitioned in XXXX. 

Per the terms of our Mortgage Agreement, we pay our Mortgagor certain additional amounts which are to be held in escrow by the Mortgagor in an escrow account, and used by the Mortgagor to pay our homeowners insurance and property taxes. 

We received notice from our township in XX/XX/XXXX that our first quarter property taxes were not timely paid, and that interest and penalties had begun to accrue. Our Mortgage Agreement provides that in addition to being obligated to use the escrowed funds to pay our property taxes, the Mortgagor is responsible for any interest and penalties due in connection with failing to timely pay such property taxes when due. Regardless of responsibility for facilitating payment of our property taxes ( and payment of penalties and interest thereon ), we are very concerned about any consequences resulting from the Mortgagors failure to pay the amounts due, including, but not limited to, the impact on our credit score and/or potential tax liens being issued against our property. The first quarter taxes should have been paid on XX/XX/XXXX. 

I called Mr. Cooper on XX/XX/XXXX, immediately following our receipt of the late notice from our township. On the call, a representative of Mr. Cooper blamed our prior Mortgagor for not paying the first quarter property taxes. The representative said that Mr. Cooper would pay our first quarter property taxes, as well as any interest and penalties accrued in connection therewith, utilizing the funds that Mr. Cooper holds in escrow, and would, thereafter, bill our prior Mortgagor for such amounts. This process is consistent with the terms of our Mortgage Agreement. 

Despite the foregoing conversation, and contrary to the terms of our Mortgage Agreement, Mr. Cooper failed to pay our property taxes and interest and penalties accrued in connection therewith. 

In follow-up telephone conversations that I initiated in the ensuing weeks with representatives of Mr. Cooper, A representative of Mr. Cooper said that Mr. Cooper had not paid the amounts due because our township had failed to provide proper documentation and had failed to return Mr. Coopers communication requests. The Mr. Cooper representative did not indicate what documentation was missing and instead told me that the issue had to be resolved between Mr. Cooper and the township directly. Additionally, my wife visited our townships taxpayers office two ( 2 ) times to confirm that the property taxes and other charges had been paid. On each occasion, the township claimed that ( despite what we had been told by Mr. Cooper ) the township had not received any communications from Mr. Cooper and that Mr. Cooper must reach out to the township directly to pay the amounts due. In short, both our township and Mr. Cooper indicated that there was nothing that we, as the homeowners, could do to solve this issue. Nevertheless, in XX/XX/XXXX, I verified on two ( 2 ) different telephone calls with Mr. Cooper representatives that they had the correct phone number for our townships XXXX XXXX XXXX on file, in hopes that the amounts due would be promptly paid. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I called Mr. Cooper again. This time, the representative from Mr. Cooper that I spoke with indicated that Mr. Cooper did not have the past-due property tax bill on file. With my assistance, the agent was able to download a copy of the property tax bill from the townships XXXX XXXX website. The Mr. Cooper representative said that the property tax bill and other amounts due in connection therewith would be paid in full and that I should call back in a little over a week for an update. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I called Mr. Cooper to confirm that the property tax bill and other amounts due had been paid and to ask for an update on the situation. The representative that I spoke with said that Mr. Cooper had confirmed the tax bill amount due, along with the interest/penalties accrued, and that Mr. Cooper would be issuing a check to my township that week. The representative again confirmed that we would not be responsible for the interest/penalties accrued. I was told to call back in five ( 5 ) days for another update. 

As of XX/XX/XXXX, the past-due property taxes and interest and penalties accrued thereon have still not been paid by Mr. Cooper. I called Mr. Cooper on XX/XX/XXXX, and the representative I spoke with initially indicated that my repeated requests for the payment of the property taxes and other amounts due had been denied due to missing documentation. When I directed the representative to look through my file, he found the documentation and sounded confused. After being placed on hold for about ten ( 10 ) minutes, the representative came back on the line and told me that my wife and I have done all we can do with regards to this matter and that the rest of the work to resolve this matter is to be handled by the Mr. Cooper tax department. Additionally, the representative said that they are working on the issue ( despite his original claim that our request had been denied ). The representative then directed me to call back on Thursday, XX/XX/XXXX, for another update. I did, and Mr. Cooper told me that their tax department was working on it, but they blamed the prior mortgager for not paying the taxes on time. They also did not have any timeline as to when this would be handled and the agent indicated that they didn't know what else could be done. I indicated I would be filing a complaint with the CFPB and the agent understood my situation. 

At this point, we are very frustrated with the situation, and the seeming lack of urgency, attention, or competency by Mr. Cooper. There is plenty of money in the escrow account established by Mr. Cooper to pay the property taxes and other amounts due. It has now been about two ( 2 ) months since my first phone call to Mr. Cooper regarding this issue ( and over three ( 3 ) months since our Mortgage was assigned ), and the first quarter property taxes have still not paid. Such failure to pay the property taxes and interest and penalties in connection therewith is a violation of Mr. Coopers obligations under the Mortgage Agreement and disregards our repeated requests for payment. Interest and penalties continue to accrue, and my wife and I are growing increasingly concerned about a tax lien being filed against our home and/or a negative impact on our credit rating. I am hoping that this issue is resolved as soon as possible.

product: Mortgage
consumer_complaint_narrative:
Entered forbearance program on ~XX/XX/2020 for an approved 3 months ( 90 days ). We explicitly stated at onset that if the only solution upon emergence from forbearance was going to increase my mortgage payments, I wasn't interested in using the program. I was ASSURED there would be other options. 

After the first " forbearance '' approved payment statements were issued, we contacted Pennymac immediately. I had concerns regarding data on the statement ( s ) during the forbearance timeframe ( amounts stated past due, threatening letters, etc ). I repeatedly called proactively, and each time I was told " all is ok '', it's automatic, and once you emerge from the forbearance period, all will be corrected. This matter continued to grow in dollars they claimed owed - somehow they got to 4 months, when we only missed 3 payments - again, after multiple concerned calls to the department handling this process, I was ASSURED this would all be corrected. 

At the end of XXXX, I called to state I didn't need the forbearance program anymore and requested a termination of forbearance, and application to resolve the missed payments, reminding them I am unable to make higher payments. It was like pulling teeth to get them to allow me to me to exit from the program. Finally I received documents ( application ) to complete that would provide my current status, from which they could determine what solution would fit. Immediately we were told that we were approved to add the missed payments on top of the current mortgage payments, as if they never heard me the first 3x I said that wasn't an option. In a period of 45 days, I received an additional 2 " approval '' documents saying that I was going to receive a deferment, moving all missed P & I into a non-interest bearing account separate from the mortgage. The first stating we had only missed 2 payments, which elicited yet another call to them, and a few weeks later stating 4 payments were being deferred and to continue to make our payments. We had already resumed payments in XX/XX/XXXX yet called again to try and correct the timelines and # of missed payments. 

With each call, I was essentially told that this process finalization is taking around 60 days due to the high demand from distressed COVID borrowers. As time went on, into XXXX, I saw the timeline for this process, as shown on their website stuck at " final stages '', yet we continued to get threatening notes, statements showing I was 4+ months past due, etc. At this point, I was making calls 2x-4x/month to proactively resolve this issue. 

Meanwhile, and unbeknownst to me, a job situation necessitated a relocation. I put my house on the market and notified Pennymac what had happened, requesting info on how this would impact the deferral. We were told multiple times it would not have any impact, but it did present some additional difficulty regarding numbers, etc., which I understood. 

By the beginning of XXXX, the website status changed to completed, yet we had not receive formal written notice from Pennymac about process going forward. Multiple calls to customer service ( the XXXX team ) confirmed that we had been approved and they were in the process of correcting the balance sheets to reflect their contracted obligation to move the CORRECT amount into the deferral account. 

During this time, the house had been placed on the market - XXXX and sold within 14 days with a 45 day close. Title and escrow began requesting the appropriate documents from all parties : the initial payoff demand, fees, taxes, title, escrow amounts, expected payments from escrow during the contract period. Title immediately noticed that something was wrong when the first payoff demand was received with past due interest, and then the final demand included 157 days of past due interest, representing XXXX - XXXX. Please understand that the loan was in service from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX - a period of 12 months and 6 days ( not 4 months ) wherein I made 9 payments in full with an additional $ XXXX/payment. The extra 6 days in Pennymac 's calculation of {$41.00} of interest per day XXXX the period from XXXX - XXXX ) amounted to ~ {$170.00} in the overall transaction. 

Title wired the EXACT amount requested on the payment demand, still confused by large changes between the initial and final payoff demand letters that didn't reconcile with the time between the initial demand request and the final demand. Yet, this was a matter left for post close reconciliation. Again, title paid the final demand in full, wired the money and confirmed receipt on XX/XX/XXXX ( a full day before the payoff expired ). 

On XXXX, title received a very strange call from Pennymac demanding an additional ~ {$1200.00} because they had supposedly made a property tax payment on XX/XX/XXXX. Title immediately stated that this was completely irregular because the tax payment should have been calculated into the final payoff demand which expired on XXXX, because the final payoff was requested prior to the payment XXXX yet 6 days after the payment had been made ). On my account activity page, it actually showed the tax payment was made on XX/XX/XXXX - 17 days earlier. 

Somewhere shortly thereafter, Pennymac again called title demanding another 4 days of interest because the loan wasn't actually paid in full until XXXX when they received the supposed " escrow shortfall '' or the additional ~ {$1200.00}. Remember, daily interest on the FULL outstanding principle was $ XXXX/day. Pennymac demanded the FULL amount of daily interest, as if they had not received any prior wire from title essentially paying off the principal and the fraudulently calculated 157 days in past due interest. 

As I understand it, escrow accounts are separate from the P & I on the mortgage - escrow accounts don't receive interest nor are they charged interest. So title argued with them, and refused to spend more time with a PennyMac rep, again on a voice call versus a fax or written demand, who couldn't explain how this had all happened - so they paid the interest out of their own pocket so they could just move on. 

Separately, I couldn't understand why the loan wasn't closed properly on XXXX and, again, called PennyMac where I received another series of lies, fabrications, excuses, etc., each contradicting the prior - but insisting their calculations were proper and correct. Each time I ended the call with, if you can't explain these transactions, the issues, etc., how do you know they are correct and defensible? Awkward silence each time, saying they would work to get me an explanation on their calculations, but that the calculations were correct. I was never ONCE told it was a title/escrow issue. I had to call title to ask why they made so many wires to Pennymac, and initially accusing them of error ( s ). 

From the get go ( beginning of the forbearance program ) XXXX mad well over 70+ calls starting in XXXX - each handled by the SPOC XXXX the ones who handle forbearance programs and deferrals for distressed buyers ... These people are the ones who are supposed to be able to explain this stuff - the only difference from a year ago is that they had more volume due to COVID, but these processes were NOT new.

My final call to them on Friday ( XX/XX/XXXX ), a 3.5 hour long call, the XXXX SUPERVISOR stated very insistently that our Deferral had NEVER been approved and ALL prior reps were wrong, with apologies. Our response was - we have the deferment approval in writing, dated XXXX, a month after your website showed approved ( XXXX ). To which he stated that a VP had gotten involved and stated I wasn't really approved and all amounts were correct, essentially implying that the VP had stated this arbitrarily and with some amount of anger, and no explanation. This supervisor was also provided with multiple calculations showing that PennyMac was wrong, likely in violation of their contracts, and clearly in violation of multiple federal lending, consumer protections laws, and the CARES act ( suspicions confirmed by title ). 

I actually see the deferral amount being entered into my transaction history around XX/XX/XXXX ( a full month after the deferral approval appeared on the PennyMac website, 7 days after our written confirmation that the deferral had been approved, yet a full 24 hours before Pennymac knew that we were actually closing the loan based on the expiration of the final payoff demand ). The same amount was then backed out of our account some 2 weeks later!!!!! Interestingly enough, the written approval still showed FOUR MISSED PAYMENTS. 

Well, a ) it was never 4 months, and b ) they never actually processed our XXXX payment received by them on XX/XX/XXXX, in the amount of {$2500.00}. 

XXXX has now been supplied with payment history directly from our bank showing the 9 payments sent and received. Title confirms the loan only existed for 12 months and a 6 day period after the XXXX month - the latter six day amounts to about {$250.00} in interest ( XXXX payment would have been due XXXX, but late on XX/XX/XXXX ). 

After 70+ calls, proactively and then reactively, you'd think someone could explain this. Even the final supervisor we spoke with admitted that it shouldn't be this hard to reconcile but claimed that HE had more information that I was being shown on their own website 's transaction history. He also stopped short of making any direct comment that something was wrong ... A prior supervisor had already looked at this, weeks before, and stated something was clearly wrong, but couldn't determine what it was .... 

In the end, I've provided Pennymac with calculation after calculation proving that even with the small amount of information they claim we have, that their principle payoff demands were incorrect, there's no explanation on how/why we were ever considered past due during an official forbearance program, and why, upon emergency, did 3 months of interest on the forbearance protected payments ( approx. {$3600.00} ) become $ XXXX dollars and 5+ months. The final supervisor stated it was because starting in XXXX, we hadn't been current : meaning my XXXX Payment applied to XXXX, the XXXX payment applied to XXXX, and the XXXX payment applied to XXXX. Still, showing the maximum amount we were EVER past due was 90 days, and still contractually protected from being considered late under the approved forbearance and the latter approved deferral. 

The outstanding principal shown on Pennymac 's website 100 % reconciled with the correct outstanding principal amount throughout the loan, until XX/XX/XXXX - when it became clear the XX/XX/XXXX payment was never applied. 

Title is now involved and will likely get involved with any civil or criminal lawsuits against Pennymac. Title clearly stated that the way this appears, and the lack of knowledge on the part of the department who is supposed to be responsible for this 24/7, proves we are NOT an isolated incident. 

In reading over other pending litigation, including 2 class action suits, etc., against PennyMac this behavior does appear systemic but with slight nuances. All of these lawsuits seem to imply that PennyMac 's goal was to find a way to foreclose, any way they could - even successfully, in some cases - destroying people 's credit, lives, etc.

Pennymac has a banner on their website I paraphrase as " We're here to help. '' That's just another lie. They claim they are researching things, but clearly not doing a thing - just appeasing us with people who say untruthful things, implying the fault is on the borrower in a nice way, like that would make any intelligent person just go away. 

How many people have been a victim to this, especially during COVID, without even realizing it and being convinced by narratives that contradict themselves to try and get them to go away .... shameful. 

Please also remember - Pennymac, as is stated at the beginning of every call, both when the XXXX answers as well as when the reps finally pick up, that they record all calls. Bank of America gave me a incorrect exchange rate ( in the bank 's favor ) for at least five transactions that I made in XXXX during a three-week trip in XXXX this year with my US BOA card. 

I know that the exchange rate was wrong because the BOA representative told me that exchange rates are handled by Visa and a Visa representative checked the rate for me. But the Visa representative said that to get a refund, I needed to go back to BOA. When I sent back to BOA, I was told that I needed to use an online process for reporting the error. 

The representative knew that I wanted to dispute every single transaction in a month of travel, since my suspicion was that if two charges checked at random were wrong, all of them might be. However, when I tried using the online process, I discovered after disputing the first three of my transactions, I was directed to call customer support. I called again and they said that they could not resolve the problem. 

They could not explain why I had been overcharged and suggested several incorrect reasons. ( One was that the rate is not the date of the transaction but the date of settlement, but I determined that this is not the problem by confirming with the agent what the rate for the date of settlement was ; the agent suggested that I was confused because there is a transaction fee of 1 %. this was also not the problem because the 1 % fee is a separate line item on the bill. finally the agent suggested that I was not taking into account a possible value added tax. This was also not an explanation because I have a copy of the exact amount in XX/XX/XXXXcurrency that the merchant charged the credit card. If there was any taxes, it would have been included already in this number. ) The agent sent me to a manager who told me that there was no remedy other than making a complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which is what I'm doing. I realize that it might be possible for me to dispute three more transactions as I did before, after some cooling off period ( but I don't know how long that would be ) and then three more and so on until I have disputed all of the approximately two dozen transactions. But there should be a better way. I have received refunds for the three transactions that I disputed ( I entered the transactions to dispute in chronological order ; these did not include the two transactions that the Visa representative previously confirmed were incorrect ; I expected I would get to them in order, but they were later in my trip, so I have not yet disputed them ). I would like BOA to recalculate every transcation I made during this trip ( which was in XXXX ). consumer_complaint_narrative:
This is a reply to the CFPB via # XXXX please be advised Under the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and Consumer Protection Act, the CFPB has the authority to take action against institutions violating consumer financial laws, including engaging in unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. The Bureau found that Edfinancial violated the Consumer Financial Protection Act by engaging in deceptive acts and practices. Edfinancial encouraged borrowers to reach out to it for help managing their student loans, and it indicated that it was an expert and could assist borrowers navigating complex student-loan repayment options. FFELP borrowers reasonably relied on Edfinancial to act in their best interests by providing them with complete and accurate information about how to qualify for PSLF and about all the available forgiveness options. Specifically, the company harmed student loan borrowers by : Misrepresenting that FFELP borrowers could not receive PSLF : When borrowers with FFELP loans asked about PSLF, Edfinancial, in many instances, told them they were ineligible, and the company did not tell them they could become eligible by consolidating their loans into Direct Loans and meeting other qualifying requirements. Sometimes, Edfinancial falsely told borrowers their FFELP loans could not be consolidated. These statements, misrepresentations, and omissions created the false impression for borrowers with FFELP loans that they could not obtain PSLF.

Misrepresenting that FFELP borrowers were making payments towards PSLF before loan consolidation : Edfinancial, in both explicit and implicit statements, told borrowers that their payments on FFELP loans would count toward the 10 years of monthly payments required to obtain PSLF. Many borrowers were likely led to believe they were making progress toward PSLF when in fact they were not because they had not consolidated their FFELP loans into Direct Loans.

Misrepresenting to borrowers that certain jobs were not eligible for PSLF : In numerous instances, Edfinancial explicitly stated that certain jobs would not qualify for PSLF when they in fact did. In other instances, Edfinancial failed to include entire job categories, such as non-profit work, when discussing PSLF qualifying jobs. Edfinancials statements likely caused many eligible borrowers to not consider PSLF as a forgiveness possibility.

Describing forgiveness programs to FFELP borrowers without mentioning PSLF : When FFELP borrowers asked about forgiveness options available to them, Edfinancial representatives often described forgiveness options available only for FFELP loans and failed to mention PSLF. The companys statements and omissions created the impression that PSLF was not an option for many FFELP borrowers. FFELP borrowers may have elected not to pursue PSLF because they were either unaware of PSLF or did not think the program applied to them.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 ) says ( 1 ) The banking system is dependent upon fair and accurate credit reporting. Inaccurate credit reports directly impair the efficiency of the banking system, and unfair credit reporting methods undermine the public confidence which is essential to the continued functioning of the banking system.

So whenever there is a violation under the FCRA, it impairs the efficiency of the banking system. This is a violation of my privacy with my consumer report, since I control what is listed and what is not. In the event that any accounts are reported without my written consent, that is considered identity theft.

This is a violation of both 15 U.S. Code 1681b ( 2 ) and 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2. This leads way to civil liability against the credit reporting agency for negligent and willful noncompliance under 15 U.S. Code 1681n, which allows for {$1000.00} per violation, for account listed without my expressed written consent.

product: Checking or savings account
consumer_complaint_narrative:
I have a joint HSBC checking account with my daughter, who lives out of the country. On XX/XX/2019 her wallet was stolen from her ( cross body ) purse on a bus in XXXX. She immediately told me and I helped her contact all the entities that might be impacted. Included in the wallet was an ATM debit card from the HSBC account which she had never used. There was a note on the card with the PIN, which I had given her ( and told her to take off! ). There were no translators available by the time she tried to go the same night, so the next day, XX/XX/2019, she went to a local police station and made a theft report. She included the HSBC ATM card in the report listing what was in the wallet that was stolen. Meanwhile the card was used 5 times in XXXX at ATM ( s? ) for withdrawals adding up to {$1000.00}. 

I contacted HSBC on her behalf on XX/XX/2019 to contest those withdrawals as unauthorized. A few days later, dated XX/XX/2019, she received a Fraud Claim Form to complete. I filled it out for her, but it required a signature, so I called HSBC who said I could sign it for her. I did so, sent it back and attached the police report. A day later, but dated XX/XX/2019, we received a letter that the case had been closed and the transactions were found to be authorized! 

I then called again, requested the documentation as the letter stated would be provided, asked that the case be reopened in light of the police report, which apparently hadn't been received when it was closed. Then followed weeks and months of calls and emails during which I was promised many things, including a provisional credit of the {$1000.00}. 

I contacted the Assistant VP who had originally opened my account, XXXX XXXX, via phone ( XXXX ) and email ( XXXX ) on numerous occasions to ask his help. I called the Fraud department ( XXXX ) numerous times and each time was told it was being investigated, but no, I couldn't speak to the investigator, etc. 

I did some research of my own on the CFPB website, and brought to XXXX 's attention Comment 6 ( b ) -2 of Regulation E which specifically addressed writing the PIN on a piece of paper kept with a debit card, and that it does NOT impose greater liability than is permissible under Regulation E. I asked XXXX to forward this to the investigator and Legal Dept and was told he did so. 

After I was finally promised the provisional credit by XX/XX/XXXX, by a supposed supervisor who gave his name as XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ). I sent a very detailed email to XXXX outlining what I had been told, what I had said and what I was requesting he do. That was sent on XX/XX/2019. I have to this date, XX/XX/2019, never heard from XXXX again. 

Having gotten no response from XXXX, I contacted the Vice President and Senior Branch Manager, XXXX XXXX, XXXX We had a conversation in late XXXX, XXXX XXXX ) and I forwarded to him all the numerous emails I had sent to XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) He was much better about keeping me informed. Ultimately I received a voicemail from XXXX on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX asking me to call him back. When I did so within 30 minutes, he told me he " regretfully '' had to tell me that the case had been denied again, but that he was authorized to " split the difference '', and offer me {$500.00}. He said he had " taken it to senior leadership '' and they were in agreement that HSBC was not responsible due to " negligence in having the PIN with the card ''. I was, of course, furious. 

I asked if he had spoken with the Legal Department and what their answer was to the law I had cited. He said they had. I asked for the documentation supporting their decision, which I had still never received about the first letter. I made it clear I wanted specific legal authority, including citations, and the facts supporting the decision. I told him that they were making a discretionary decision that was NOT supported by the law. I also asked for the name of a higher level person to whom to appeal. 

Meanwhile I told him I would think about his offer. He sent me an email on XX/XX/XXXX stating that he had spoken to the " fraud and client escalation teams and a letter is being drafted to you explaining the reason for the denied fraud claim ''. 

About a week later I received a letter dated XX/XX/2019 with the EXACT same wording as the first letter, with the name of XXXX XXXX ( it was not signed ). There was no explanation of the declination, no supporting documentation or law cited. There was NOTHING supporting the denial of the fraud claim. Again it said we could contact the sender, at the same number as the first letter. 

I have all the emails I sent, and sent to me. I have the XXXX Police Report, a copy of the Fraud Claim Report I submitted, as well as the two letters denying the claim. I also have names and dates and times of all the many calls I made. I am happy to provide any and all information needed.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
In late XXXX/early XXXX, we received a mailing from Freedom Mortgage, a company affiliated with our current mortgage holder, XXXX XXXX. The mailing stated that Freedom works with current XXXX customers to reduce their interest rate and lower their monthly payments. 

On or about XX/XX/XXXX, we spoke with Loan Officer XXXX XXXX. XXXX asked us some general questions ; are we married, do we own the home ; is it our primary residence, etc. He asked no questions related to the style of home we live in. 
We had some email correspondence clarifying some questions and concerns. XXXX clearly stated that if we started now, that we would likely close in XXXX and that instead of making my XXXX mortgage payment on the XX/XX/XXXX, we would be bring with us to closing the interest and taxes as our payment ( Exhibit 1 ). 

On or about that same date, XXXX sent us the Loan Estimate ( Exhibit 2 ). After reviewing the estimated documents, we entered into an agreement with Freedom to move forward with streamline refinance. After XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX never willingly contacted us again, with the exception of 2 auto-generated form emails. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, we received an email statement from our current mortgage company, which included the requested payoff quote ( Exhibit 3 ). As this would be a normal step in the process, we assumed that everything was moving forward accordingly. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a call from XXXX XXXX, a Customer Advocate for Freedom Mortgage. During this call it was discovered that XXXX had provided me with wrong information. During my XX/XX/XXXX call with XXXX, he told me that I would need to provide a Utility Bill that showed my address. I disclosed to XXXX that we do not get mail delivered to our physical address ; everything goes to our PO Box . I explained the reason and XXXX said " that is not a problem - worst case we will have you send a letter explaining why you don't get mail at your physical address ''. Turns out, that was a problem. Freedom Mortgage stated that in order to proceed, I had to provide a utility bill that had my physical address as my mailing address. They would not accept a bill that showed " for service at '' and then my physical address. Ok. Fine. We worked with our utility company and made the change and sent the utility bill over. That was accepted by XXXX on XX/XX/19. I have had no additional communication with XXXX since that time ( Exhibit 4 ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a auto-generated form email from XXXX XXXX ( Exhibit 5 ). This email contained documents that required our signature. One of the documents was the Closing Disclosure ( Exhibit 6 ). This Closing Disclosure specifically states " This form is a statement of final loan terms and closing costs. Compare this document with your Loan Estimate. '' This Closing Disclosure stated that closing would take place on XX/XX/19, with the loan funding on XX/XX/19. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, in the later part of the afternoon, I received a call from XXXX XXXX ( unsure of her role -- maybe the loan processor?? ). XXXX explained that either XXXX entered the property detail incorrectly or he failed to ask the proper questions to establish what type of property we own ( we have a manufactured home on the property ). Because it is a manufactured home, they would need to reopen title, which would then require the title review and the legal department to review. This would delay the closing a few weeks. 

I asked if this would change the Closing Statement that I received. It was at this point that I found out that Freedom Mortgage does not consider the Closing Statement that they sent me Final, as it is not " Final '' until closing. Of course, nobody called me to explain this to me. I had the Closing Statement for almost 2 weeks before a single person reached out to me -- and they only reached out because a mistake was made. 

At this same time, XXXX asked XXXX XXXX to reach out to me to explain things. He called me and basically accused me of lying, as " surely he explained these things to me '', even though I had not one single personal communication from XXXX in almost a month. However, of specific mention, on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX put in writing that the closing team should have gone over the closing disclosure information and apologizes for that they did not. Further, he admits that he did not confirm the property type with me and that he should have ( Exhibit 7 ). 

I have had numerous email messages with XXXX and her supervisor, XXXX. Of most importance, is the email from XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX in which she admits that Freedom Mortgage input the property type from the beginning and apologizes for the way my " file '' has been handled. Then again on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX apologizes for for the times that I did not receive the level of service that I deserve ( Exhibit 8 ). 

XXXX and XXXX both assured me that the would keep me informed of the progress. However, on XX/XX/XXXX, the Title Company reached out to me asking for additional information. I had no idea that that title company had sent an email, as the email landed in my Junk Folder. Neither XXXX or XXXX attempted to contact me in any form on XX/XX/XXXX to let me know about this development ( even though they said they would keep me updated as to progress ). It took them almost 1 week before they reached out to me, wondering why I had not responded to the title company. Had they let me know to watch for an email, I would have watched for it and would have looked at my junk folder. I would not call this keeping me up-to-date or informing me of progress ( Exhibit 9 and 10 ). 

At this point, I have no idea if the loan will close or how much this is costing me. So far, it has cost me an additional {$900.00}. XXXX and XXXX are telling me that they can not provide me with an updated Loan Estimate, as they need me to make my XXXX house payment first ( cost : {$3000.00} ), but this is the one that XXXX said would only cost me ( {$2100.00} ). XXXX was able to get me a Loan Estimate within an hour of me stating we wanted to move forward, but it is going to take XXXX a few weeks?? 

I have some serious doubts ... ....

A full itemized breakdown of the amount owed, including any interest or fees added. 
Any contract, agreement, or documentation bearing my signature that confirms my obligation to pay this debt. 
Proof that they are licensed to collect in Tennessee and are in compliance with applicable state and federal laws. 
A copy of the initial notice they were required to send within five days of first contact.

P & B Capital Group has failed to provide any of this requested documentation.

Since they have not validated this debt, I believe this collection should not be reported to XXXX and request that the CFPB investigate this issue. Additionally, their failure to provide prior notice deprived me of my legal right to dispute the debt before it was reported to my credit file. 

I request that the CFPB : Investigate whether P & B Capital Group provided proper debt validation before reporting this account. 
Ensure that P & B Capital Group ceases collection and removes the account from my credit report if they can not provide proper validation.

Require P & B Capital Group to provide a full and accurate accounting of the debt, including proof of ownership and the original creditors details.

I am also considering filing additional complaints with the Tennessee Collection Service Board, the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), and the Tennessee Attorney Generals Office if this issue is not resolved promptly.

( 2 ) An elaborate mechanism has been developed for investigating and evaluating the credit worthiness, credit standing, credit capacity, character, and general reputation of consumers.

( 4 ) There is a need to insure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy.

( b ) Reasonable procedures It is the purpose of this subchapter to require that consumer reporting agencies adopt reasonable procedures for meeting the needs of commerce for consumer credit, personnel, insurance, and other information in a manner which is fair and equitable to the consumer, with regard to the confidentiality, accuracy, relevancy, and proper utilization of such information in accordance with the requirements of this subchapter.

a ) Identity and purposes of credit users Every consumer reporting agency shall maintain reasonable procedures designed to avoid violations of section 1681c of this title and to limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b of this title. These procedures shall require that prospective users of the information identify themselves, certify the purposes for which the information is sought, and certify that the information will be used for no other purpose. Every consumer reporting agency shall make a reasonable effort to verify the identity of a new prospective user and the uses certified by such prospective user prior to furnishing such user a consumer report. No consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report to any person if it has reasonable grounds for believing that the consumer report will not be used for a purpose listed in section 1681b of this title.

( b ) Accuracy of report Whenever a consumer reporting agency prepares a consumer report it shall follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of the information concerning the individual about whom the report relates.

( c ) Disclosure of consumer reports by users allowed A consumer reporting agency may not prohibit a user of a consumer report furnished by the agency on a consumer from disclosing the contents of the report to the consumer, if adverse action against the consumer has been taken by the user based in whole or in part on the report.

( d ) Notice to users and furnishers of information ( 1 ) Notice requirement A consumer reporting agency shall provide to any person ( A ) who regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to the agency with respect to any consumer ; or ( B ) to whom a consumer report is provided by the agency ; a notice of such persons responsibilities under this subchapter.

( 2 ) Content of notice The Bureau shall prescribe the content of notices under paragraph ( 1 ), and a consumer reporting agency shall be in compliance with this subsection if it provides a notice under paragraph ( 1 ) that is substantially similar to the Bureau prescription under this paragraph.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
Subject : Formal Dispute and Immediate Demand for Deletion of Unauthorized Reporting To Whom It May Concern, This letter serves as a formal dispute and demand for immediate removal of unauthorized and unlawful information being reported by your agency on my consumer report. Your actions violate federal laws and infringe on my rights as a consumer. The continued furnishing and reporting of my private financial information is illegal under multiple sections of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ), and other consumer protection laws.

Violations Committed by Your Agency 1. Violation of Consumer Privacy ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 Section 602 ( a ) ) The FCRA mandates that consumer reporting agencies must exercise their responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and respect for consumer privacy. However, Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion have failed to uphold this legal obligation by disclosing my financial data without my consent.

2. No Written Authorization to Furnish My Consumer Report ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 Section 604 ( a ) ( 2 ) ) Under 15 U.S. Code 1681b, a consumer report may only be furnished with the written instructions of the consumer. I have never provided written consent for Equifax, Experian, or TransUnion to report or share my information with third parties. Any and all prior consent is hereby revokedwhether verbal, written, implied, or otherwise.

3. Violation of My Right to Opt-Out ( 12 CFR 1016.7 ) Federal regulations grant consumers the absolute right to opt out of having their nonpublic personal information disclosed. I am formally exercising my right to opt out, and you are required to comply under federal law.

4. Failure to Notify Me of My Right to Non-Disclosure ( 15 U.S. Code 6802 ( b ) ( c ) ) The GLBA mandates that financial institutions must inform consumers of their right to prevent disclosure of nonpublic personal information. I was never given such an option, rendering the reporting of my information illegal. 5. Reporting of Obsolete Adverse Information ( 15 U.S. Code 1681c ( a ) ( 5 ) ) The FCRA strictly prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including adverse
information older than seven years ( except for criminal convictions ). The negative accounts being reported by your agencies either exceed the statutory reporting period or are being re-reported improperly, violating my rights under federal law.

6. Knowingly Reporting Inaccurate Information ( 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) ) Under 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2, no entity may furnish consumer information to a credit reporting agency if they know or have reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. The furnisher of information has failed to ensure the accuracy of the data, and your agencies have failed to conduct proper procedures to validate its accuracy before reporting it.

7. Failure to Maintain Reasonable Procedures to Ensure Accuracy ( 15 U.S. Code 1681e ( b ) ) Consumer reporting agencies must maintain reasonable procedures to avoid violations of 15 U.S. Code 1681c and ensure that consumer reports are only furnished for legally authorized purposes. Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion are failing to comply with this law.

Demand for Immediate Action Due to your blatant disregard for federal consumer protection laws, I demand the following actions be taken IMMEDIATELY : 1. Permanent deletion of any and all disputed information that has been furnished or reported without my written authorization.

2. A formal written confirmation from Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion verifying the deletion of the disputed items from my consumer report. 
3. A full disclosure of any third parties that have accessed my consumer report without my explicit consent.

4. Cessation of any further reporting of my personal information without my express written consent.

Failure to comply within 30 days from receipt of this letter will result in my immediate pursuit of legal action against Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, and any other responsible parties. I will not hesitate to file complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), and my states Attorney Generals Office if my rights continue to be violated.

This is your final opportunity to comply before I escalate this matter to federal regulators and legal authorities. Please provide a written response confirming the deletion of the disputed items no later than 30 days from receipt of this letter.

This is a formal demand for immediate correction and legal compliance regarding the improper reporting of a bankruptcy on my consumer report in clear violation of federal laws, specifically 15 USC 1681b ( 2 ), 15 USC 1681q, 18 USC 1028A, and 15 USC 1681c-2. Your agencys unlawful actions constitute a direct violation of my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and criminal statutes protecting consumer information.

Violation of 15 USC 1681b ( 2 ) Unauthorized Access to My Consumer Report Pursuant to 15 USC 1681b ( 2 ), you are prohibited from obtaining or furnishing my consumer report without permissible purpose and my explicit consent. The inclusion of a bankruptcy on my report, which I did not authorize nor was it obtained with my direct consent, constitutes an unlawful access and use of my personal credit data.

Violation of 15 USC 1681q Obtaining Consumer Report Under False Pretenses Furthermore, under 15 USC 1681q, any entity that obtains a consumer report under false pretenses is subject to severe penalties. If your agency has accessed or furnished my report to third parties without lawful grounds, this constitutes fraud and deception under federal law. product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
consumer_complaint_narrative:
To Whom it may concern, I am filing this complaint after failed attempts to gain clarity or an understanding of the information contained in my Lexis Nexis report. After being denied and/or rejected coverage for both auto and homeowners insurance without any clear understanding as to why, I began to investigate the cause. In fairness, I have had a couple traffic infractions although, I couldnt see why that would be a cause for denial of homeowners insurance. I have had a consistent credit score in the mid XXXX over the last 24 months and never once filed a homeowners claim with any of my previous homes. 

So, after requesting my Lexis Nexis risk report twice and reviewing the wealth of personal information it contains about me, I came across an entry that caught my attention. It was an annotation on my report requested by State Farm Mut and prepared by Lexis Nexis that I found odd since I hadnt requested any insurance from XXXX XXXX ever. Even more peculiar, it was associated with my former spouses information and had portions of our DOBs and included my address listed as the same as hers even though, we hadnt lived together since XXXX. Our official record of dissolution is dated XX/XX/XXXX. 

I further discovered on my XXXX/Risk report was an insurance claim paid out on behalf of my former spouse with my name associated to the claim which included my partial DOB and other personal information of mine and again, had my address associated with hers giving the appearance we were residing at the same address.

The XXXX/Risk report Lexis Nexis provides to insurance companies and other affiliated organizations consists of an extensive amount of personal information and proves extremely challenging to decipher. Understandably, I contacted Lexis Nexis to inquire about these entries and some much needed assistance to understand the rationale of why my former spouses information would be included in my XXXX/Risk report and if maybe I was somehow misinterpreting the data it contained. 

Unfortunately, I was given little understanding as to why that information was there other than the insurance company had requested a search of that data and that was why it was listed on my XXXXRisk report. When I informed the individual, I never inquired about insurance via XXXX XXXX, I was then told your former spouse must have requested it. I then asked well why did they have my DOB included in a search for my ex-wife, if I wasnt the specific one requesting the insurance to which, I did not get a clear answer or explanation.

I sought out Lexis Nexis for assistance and clarity on information that they collect in the aggregate then compile and provide to companies for a fee so these companies can make a business decision which determines what a customer will be charged for their service. Lexis Nexis chose to ignore my concerns, providing me half-truths to legitimate questions and ultimately hung up on me when they did not have a reasonable or logical answer as to why certain information was include on my report.

It states on my report, Insurers use prior loss information in the underwriting and rating of automobile insurance policies. This report is not a recommendation insurance companies utilize prior loss information in accordance with their own underwriting guidelines.

Given that statement, it would lead one to believe, if a claim was paid out on behalf of my former spouse yet somehow it was included on my XXXX/Risk report, its highly likely to be viewed negatively by any potential insurance companies I may have sought out, during that period. It would also give the perception that I might be a higher risk client and therefore, be a cause for denial. Yet, Lexis Nexis attempted to state that it was the insurance company who elicited the search, not their organization, and they are only reporting on the vast and extensive amount of data they continuously collect daily on any given individual in the country.

I would further like to point out that I did not solicit State Farm Mut for any of their services in my quest to gain auto or homeowners insurance however, Lexis Nexis states, that is the company who initiated the search and is the cause for my former spouses information being associated with mine on my XXXX/Risk report, despite not having my consent to use my personal information to search for previously filed insurance claims or to have my personal information included with my ex-wifes search for insurance. Its a clear case of unauthorized use of my personal information and which was used for reasons I am unaware of, except for the evidence of it being on my report. 

Both Lexis Nexis and XXXX XXXX Mut were careless and reckless, showing little, if any concern of who was the initiator or requested the search for this information. If this is the position Lexis Nexis takes and they only report on the data they collect, dont they have some level of responsibility or due diligence to the consumer to confirm the search request is valid and has the consumers consent?? 

After speaking with a CSR at Lexis Nexis, none of it made sense and I was left with the realization that the company, who the consumer is relying on to assist and help with corrections or potential misrepresented data, claimed everything listed on my XXXX/Risk report was standard practice and nothing out of the ordinary has occurred although, I have insurance denials that lead me to believe otherwise and a copy of my report that contains questionable entries related to me ex-wife and when I inquired about this, I was lead to believe it's a standard search requested by insurance companies that routinely occurs despite, once again, informing them, I did not approach, request, solicit, or inquire, with that specific company for any insurance products so my approval and consent was never given for this action. 

Both organizations are doing a huge disservice to the consumer and neither care to correct misrepresented information or at a minimum, provide a reasonable response as to why certain data of my ex-wife 's is associated and included in my individual XXXX/Risk report. 

Therefore, I am filing this complaint on both State Farm Mutual and Lexis Nexis for their lack of permissible purpose for requesting and subsequently, providing my consumer risk report without my valid consent which is a violation of FCRAs sections 604 ( a ) ( 3 ) and ( f ) provisions. I was not the subject of the users request and yet Lexis Nexis chose to include my information in a search requested by XXXX XXXX mutual when I did not provide nor give my consent. 

I thank you for your time and Im sorry this was so verbose. I am available to discuss this matter further, as needed and encourage you to contact me via the information I have provided. Again, thank you and have a terrific day!! 

Respectfully, XXXX

This new representative then denied me for all loss-mitigation options, including home-retention options, without requesting or reviewing any income documentation, despite my self-employed status. 

No income analysis, affordability calculation, or FHA worksheet was provided. No explanation was given as to how eligibility was determined without financial review.

3. Appeal Reviewed and Denied by the Same Individual Without Income Review I timely appealed the denial, submitting the appeal as permitted under FHA guidelines. 

The appeal was then reviewed and denied by the same individual who issued the original denial, with no independent review and again without any income documentation review. 

The denial cited insufficient number of payments since loan origination as the basis for denying all FHA loss-mitigation options, despite : No income analysis being conducted No evaluation of FHA partial claim plus modification No sustainable payment determination No written explanation of how this criterion was applied or whether exceptions were considered Denying all loss-mitigation options based on this factor without reviewing income and without independent appeal review constitutes a procedurally defective and non-compliant FHA evaluation. 

4. Foreclosure Activity Continued During Active Appeal Period ( Dual Tracking ) While my appeal rights remained open through XX/XX/XXXX, Selene XXXX continued foreclosure activity, including assessing new foreclosure attorney and title search fees on XX/XX/XXXX, as reflected on my XX/XX/XXXX mortgage statement. 

Proceeding with foreclosure actions while a borrower is within an FHA loss-mitigation appeal period constitutes impermissible dual tracking. 

Why This Is a Problem FHA loss-mitigation decisions were issued without any income documentation review A partial claim was offered without assessing affordability All options were later denied without income review The appeal was denied by the same individual, with no independent reconsideration Foreclosure actions continued during an active appeal window These actions deprived me of FHA-mandated procedural protections and materially increased arrears Foreclosure activity taken against an owner-occupied FHA borrower who is actively seeking to retain their primary residence and exercising appeal rights undermines the purpose of FHA loss-mitigation requirements and consumer-protection safeguards Selene XXXX XXXX has stated that a property valuation ( written appraisal or property evaluation ) was obtained and uploaded to the borrower portal in connection with my loss-mitigation review. 

However, when I accessed the borrower portal, no appraisal or property valuation report is available, and no copy has ever been provided to me despite repeated review of the portal.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
My mortgage was recently transferred to Truist on XX/XX/year>. When attempting to set up access to view and pay my mortgage, I was informed that I am required to ( XXXX ) open a Truist checking account and ( XXXX ) agree to a mandatory arbitration clause waiving my right to sue before I am allowed to access or make payments on my mortgage. I can not access my account or pay my mortgage unless I accept these agreements, as shown in the screenshot, and I also can't open a convo with them until I have access to my portal by signing these. 

Mortgage servicers are required under federal law ( RESPA, Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024 ) to provide access to account information and payment processing without requiring the customer to accept unrelated products or legal-right waivers. 

Additionally, under the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act ( 5 M.R.S. 205-A et seq. ), it is unlawful to condition access to a required service ( mortgage servicing ) on the acceptance of unrelated financial products or the waiver of consumer legal rights. 

I am being prevented from accessing my mortgage unless I sign an online banking agreement that contains a forced arbitration clause. Access to legally required mortgage servicing functions can not be conditioned on waiving my right to sue. 

When I posted on reddit to see if other people had similar issues, an individual who appeared to have inside knowledge of Truist policies and seemed to be a Truist employee based on their reddit history attempted to discourage me from asserting my rights and claim I could just put a XXXX in the account. This raises concerns regarding whether Truist employees or agents are giving misleading or discouraging information in public forums. 

I am requesting the CFPB ensure that : XXXX. I am provided immediate access to my mortgage account and payment options without being required to open a checking account ; XXXX. I am allowed to opt out of the arbitration clause while still accessing basic servicing functions ; XXXX. Truist documents my opt-out and allows me to manage and pay my mortgage without forced product enrollment or legal waiver.

I am writing to file a complaint against TransUnion regarding their failure to appropriately respond to my dispute regarding inaccuracies on my credit report.

Additionally, I disputed incorrect personal information listed on my credit report. I ensured to include a copy of my photo ID, social security card, and a recent bill with my current address to assist TransUnion in verifying my identity and address. 

I received a response from TransUnion dated XX/XX/2024, stating that they had received my request, but it didn't appear that I or a properly authorized third party had sent it to them. Subsequently, I spoke with a supervisor named XXXX, who indicated that TransUnion had reason to believe the documents were coming from a credit repair company. However, when I asked for specifics, XXXX stated that TransUnion could identify this internally and refused to process my dispute further. This response is not only frustrating but also a violation of my rights under the FCRA. 

According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information in a consumer 's file at a credit bureau is disputed by the consumer, the bureau must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate. It is evident that TransUnion has failed to conduct a reasonable investigation upon receipt of my dispute, as required by law.

Despite multiple written requests for correction ( letters dated XX/XX/year> and XX/XX/year> ), my requests have been ignored, constituting a violation of multiple federal statutes, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). 
Violations Committed : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations : Under 15 U.S. Code 1666b, creditors must send periodic statements at least 21 days before the payment due date. The continued reporting of this inaccurate late payment demonstrates a failure to comply with this requirement.

15 U.S. Code 1681i mandates that credit reporting agencies ensure the accuracy of consumer credit files. In my case, this obligation has not been upheld.

15 U.S. Code 1681e ( b ) requires that consumer reporting agencies maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy in credit reports.

15 U.S. Code 1681a ( d ) ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ) states that certain transactions and experiences should not be considered part of a consumer report if they do not meet specific criteria.

Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) Violations : The TILA emphasizes the necessity of accurate and timely disclosures to consumers. The wrongful reporting of a late payment has damaged my creditworthiness, causing undue financial harm.

Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ) Violations : 15 U.S. Code 6801, 15 U.S. Code 6802, and 15 U.S. Code 6803 require financial institutions to protect consumer privacy and ensure the accuracy of financial reporting. The mishandling of my credit information suggests a failure to meet these obligations.

Protection Against Non-Payment of Obligations Act ( PAANL ) : This act holds creditors accountable for providing timely statements and preventing unfair penalties. The continued presence of this late payment on my report contradicts this protection.

Identity Fraud and Misreporting - 18 U.S. Code 1028A : The continued reporting of false information could be classified as a misrepresentation of identity or fraudulent reporting, which carries legal consequences under federal law.

If this issue is not resolved immediately, I will escalate my complaint further, including potential legal action and filing additional complaints with relevant agencies.

Perhaps this is the way of student loan lenders, but if so, something needs to change. However, I do hope that this submission can be taken seriously, and that we as a culture and society can begin to realize the weight of student loans and the adverse effects of that weight on our entire economy. product: Credit card or prepaid card
consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/2020 I booked a hotel in XXXX that required full prepayment. Before making the purchase, I logged into my Chase credit card account to do research about whether my account charged foreign transaction fees or not. The decision I would make on which credit card to use for my purchase was contingent on this information. 

I logged into the website and, while still logged into my account, I navigated to the " Things You Can Do '' menu, selecting " Card Benefits '' as the option. 

Doing this opened a new window, seemingly outlining all of the benefits of my card ( since this was auto-navigated from the card benefits section of my logged-in menu selection ). 

From there, I continued my research selecting " Travel Benefits '' from the page 's menu. Upon clicking that option, the first benefit highlighted was " {$0.00} Foreign Transaction Fees ''. Upon reading this, I decided to use my Chase card to make the purchase, confident that I would not be charged a foreign transaction fee for doing so. 

Imagine my surprise when on XX/XX/2020 I noted a {$210.00} foreign transaction fee for the hotel prepayment. I immediately sent Chase a message via their secure messaging center asking them to remove the erroneous fee. They responded saying that my card did, in fact, charge a fee of 3 % for any foreign transactions and so the fee was correct. 

I replied, explaining that the website clearly showed there was no fee for my card. I also sent screen shots of the navigation steps that I took to arrive at that information. They informed me that the links took me to the wrong card type, in spite of the links opening from my own account page. They apologized for the mis-information but would not reverse the fee. 

I insisted that this was an error on their side given that I made a logical determination of an action based on the information their own website provided me but they will not refund the fee. 

My position is that this is clearly misleading and intentionally providing consumers with incorrect information about their fees for their cards. No reasonable person would assume that by seeking out cardmember benefits from their account page while logged in would be directed to a page about a different type of card with different fees. Further, in spite of the fact that I've informed Chase of this mis-information and broken link, they still have not corrected the information. This leads me to believe it is intentional and that other consumers will fall prey to the same error as I have This is unacceptable and action should be taken immediately.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
consumer_complaint_narrative:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to request your assistance in resolving an ongoing issue with Experian regarding the correction and updating of my credit profile. 

On three separate occasions, I sent certified returned receipt letters to Experian requesting updates to my credit profile with the correct information. Each of these requests included three forms of proof of my identity : my ID, my social security card, and proof of address. Despite providing all the necessary documentation, Experian has repeatedly denied my right to correct or update my credit profile. 

Below is an example of Experian 's response to my request : -- - **XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ** " We received a recent request regarding your credit information that does not appear to have been sent directly by you or to be authorized by you. As a precautionary measure, we have not taken any action on your alleged request. According to the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, 'if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information contained in a consumer 's file at a national consumer credit reporting company is disputed by the consumer and the consumer notifies the company directly of such dispute, the company shall reinvestigate free of charge. ' Therefore, you can dispute any inaccurate information directly with Experian for free. 

If you believe that information in your personal credit report is inaccurate or incomplete, please call us at the phone number XXXX, or visit our secure website to upload your documents at www.experian.com/dispute. '' -- - Despite following their instructions and providing all required documents, my requests have been consistently denied. My most recent attempt to fix my report was on XX/XX/2024, yet I still have not received a satisfactory resolution. I am now seeking the involvement of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to ensure that this matter is resolved appropriately and to prevent any further unnecessary trauma. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) is the U.S. federal law that promotes the accuracy, fairness, and privacy of consumer information contained in the files of consumer reporting agencies. Specifically, under the FCRA, consumers have the right to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information in their credit reports, and the credit bureaus are required to investigate and correct any errors. 

The relevant section of the FCRA that addresses a consumer 's right to dispute and request updates to their credit profile is **Section 611**. This section is codified at **15 U.S.C . 1681i** and details the procedures for disputing the accuracy of information in a consumer 's file.

Key points of Section 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) include : 1. **Reinvestigation of Disputed Information** : When a consumer disputes the accuracy of any item of information contained in their credit report, the credit reporting agency ( CRA ) must reinvestigate free of charge and record the current status of the disputed information within 30 days, unless the CRA reasonably determines that the dispute is frivolous or irrelevant.

2. **Prompt Notice of Dispute** : The CRA must promptly notify the furnisher of the information ( such as a creditor ) of the dispute. 

3. **Correction of Errors** : If the information is found to be inaccurate or incomplete or can not be verified, the CRA must promptly delete or modify the item of information.

4. **Notification to the Consumer** : The CRA must provide the consumer with the results of the reinvestigation, a revised credit report if changes were made, and information on their right to add a statement disputing the information if the reinvestigation does not resolve the dispute. 

By utilizing these provisions, consumers can ensure that their credit reports are accurate and up-to-date. It is imperative that Experian adheres to these legal requirements to protect the rights of consumers. 

Furthermore, given that I have sent my ID, social security card, and pay stub, it is unclear how Experian could conclude that I was not sending my own request. This appears to be a stalling tactic that is both frustrating and unwarranted. 

Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.

Failure to Properly Address My Dispute I initially filed this dispute regarding the transactions and late payments on my account, which I believe to be inaccurate and unsubstantiated. However, despite my attempts to resolve these issues, the disputed items continue to be reported on my credit report, in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). According to 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ), information that is under dispute must not be reported as negative or delinquent until the investigation is complete and the dispute is resolved. 

On XX/XX/year>, I contacted American Express regarding this matter and was informed that my faxed documentation, which I sent to support my dispute, was not received. In previous communications, American Express indicated that I was locked out of the portal, which has prevented me from submitting these items in a timely manner. This is not the first time I have encountered such behavior from American Express, and it is clear that this ongoing pattern of discrimination has prevented me from receiving fair and equal treatment under the law.

Legal Obligations and Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations Under the FCRA, American Express has specific obligations to ensure that disputed information is not reported as negative or delinquent until the dispute is resolved. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), creditors are required to report accurate information to credit reporting agencies and must promptly correct any inaccuracies. 

Further, under Section 611 ( a ) of the FCRA ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), I have the right to dispute inaccurate information on my credit report directly with the credit reporting agencies. American Express is also required to investigate my dispute thoroughly and provide me with the results of that investigation. The law also requires that if the dispute is not resolved in my favor, American Express must allow me to submit a statement of my perspective to be included in my credit report. 

Moreover, under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), I am entitled to protection against unauthorized or incorrect charges. The law prohibits creditors from continuing to report a disputed charge as delinquent or negative while an investigation is still pending.

5. Addressing Discriminatory Practices : Investigate the pattern of discriminatory behavior I have encountered during this process and take appropriate action to ensure that all customers are treated fairly and without bias. 

Consequences of Non-Compliance If American Express fails to take the necessary steps to resolve this matter in a fair and lawful manner, I will have no choice but to pursue further legal action. I will also continue to document these issues and present them to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) as part of my ongoing complaint.

I expect that American Express will comply with these legal obligations and handle this dispute with the urgency and fairness it requires. Any failure to act accordingly may result in further legal action to protect my consumer rights.

" I was shocked and devastated to see credit inquiries without my knowledge. I have reached out to the creditors to ask the following but they have FAILED to provide such. 
Inquiry Details : Ask the creditor to provide specific details about the inquiry, such as the date it was made, the purpose of the inquiry and the type of credit product or service associated with the inquiry.

Application Documentation : Request copies of any credit applications or other documents related to the inquiry. This may include application forms, agreements, or disclosures that you would have completed or received when applying for credit.

Authorization Documentation : Ask the creditor to provide evidence of your authorization for the inquiry. This could include signed consent forms, agreements, or disclosures that demonstrate you provided permission for the creditor to access your credit report.

Communication Records : Request copies of any correspondence or communication between you and the creditor regarding the inquiry. This may include emails, letters, or notes documenting your interactions with the creditor.

Internal Records : Ask the creditor to provide internal records or notes related to the inquiry, including any decision-making processes or reasons for initiating the inquiry. 
Identity Verification : If identity theft is a concern, request verification measures taken by the creditor to confirm your identity before initiating the inquiry. This may include verification of personal information or identity documents provided during the application process.

Compliance Documentation : Inquire about the creditor 's compliance with relevant laws and regulations governing credit inquiries, such as the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ).

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
consumer_complaint_narrative:
I am filing this complaint against TRANSUNION, for the continued reporting of an inaccurate, unverifiable bankruptcy in my credit report. This has negatively impacted my credit profile, even though the reporting is based on improper sources, lacks verification, and violates my privacy rights. I am requesting that the CFPB intervene to enforce the immediate removal of this bankruptcy and all associated accounts from my credit report.

The reporting of this bankruptcy is inaccurate, unsubstantiated, and violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), as detailed below : 1. Inaccurate and Unverifiable Reporting ( FCRA 1681e ( b ), 15 U.S.C. 1681c ) - The FCRA requires credit reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to ensure the accuracy of reported information. Since courthouses do not directly report bankruptcy information to credit bureaus, the source of this information is unverifiable, and its continued reporting lacks a legitimate basis.

2. Unauthorized Public Dissemination of Private Information ( FCRA 1681b ) - The FCRA stipulates that credit bureaus can report consumer information only with consumer consent or for permissible purposes. I have not authorized any credit bureau to report this bankruptcy, making the current reporting of this information a violation of my privacy rights.

3. Failure to Provide Verification ( FCRA 611 ( a ) and 611 ( a ) ( 7 ) ) I disputed this bankruptcy with each credit bureau. Under FCRA 611 ( a ), credit bureaus are required to investigate within 30 days and delete unverifiable information. FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 7 ) further grants me the right to detailed information regarding the verification, including the name of the source and methodology used. The bureaus failed to provide adequate verification, and this bankruptcy should be removed.

4. Additional Violations and Potential Liability Under 15 U.S.C. 1681 ( a ) ( 4 ), the FCRA protects consumer information to avoid damaging consumers creditworthiness and reputation. Sections 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o outline liabilities for willful or negligent non-compliance with the FCRA. The continued reporting of this bankruptcy is improper and subjects these bureaus to potential liability.

17 CFR 248.124 - Reasonable opportunity to opt out.

248.124 Reasonable opportunity to opt out.

( a ) In general. You must not use eligibility information that you receive from an affiliate to make marketing solicitations to a consumer about your products or services unless the consumer is provided a reasonable opportunity to opt out, as required by 248.121 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( ii ).

( b ) Examples of a reasonable opportunity to opt out. The consumer is given a reasonable opportunity to opt out if : ( 1 ) By mail. The opt out notice is mailed to the consumer. The consumer is given 30 days from the date the notice is mailed to elect to opt out by any reasonable means.

( 2 ) By electronic means.

( i ) The opt out notice is provided electronically to the consumer, such as by posting the notice at an Internet Web site at which the consumer has obtained a product or service. The consumer acknowledges receipt of the electronic notice. The consumer is given 30 days after the date the consumer acknowledges receipt to elect to opt out by any reasonable means.

( ii ) The opt out notice is provided to the consumer by e-mail where the consumer has agreed to receive disclosures by e-mail from the person sending the notice. The consumer is given 30 days after the e-mail is sent to elect to opt out by any reasonable means.

( 3 ) At the time of an electronic transaction. The opt out notice is provided to the consumer at the time of an electronic transaction, such as a transaction conducted on an Internet Web site. The consumer is required to decide, as a necessary part of proceeding with the transaction, whether to opt out before completing the transaction. There is a simple process that the consumer may use to opt out at that time using the same mechanism through which the transaction is conducted.

( 4 ) At the time of an in-person transaction. The opt out notice is provided to the consumer in writing at the time of an in-person transaction. The consumer is required to decide, as a necessary part of proceeding with the transaction, whether to opt out before completing the transaction, and is not permitted to complete the transaction without making a choice. Lenders misleading borrowers and failing to carry out their instructions for refinancing : Refinancing or consolidating federal loans through a private lender results in the loss of important federal protections. CFPB examiners found that lenders gave misleading impressions that borrowers who refinance might not lose access to federal loan cancellation programs. Lenders also failed to re-amortize consolidated loans following borrowers requests to exclude federal loans. 
Private lenders deceiving borrowers or denying benefits : Supervision found that lenders unfairly denied discharge applications for borrowers who were eligible based on Total and Permanent Disability status. Lenders also inaccurately claimed certain borrowers were ineligible for autopay discounts or falsely advertised to borrowers that they could suspend their loan payments if they lost their job but later eliminated this benefit. 
Servicers failing to address claims related to school misconduct : Many private student loans made directly by schools include provisions allowing borrowers to challenge their loans due to school misconduct, regardless of who holds the loans. CFPB examiners found that servicers misled borrowers about their right to challenge their loans and failed to properly consider most borrowers challenges to their loans based on school misconduct. The CFPB directed the entities to create robust systems for evaluating borrowers claims of school misconduct. 
Servicers distributing contracts allowing illegal collection tactics : CFPB supervision uncovered institutional loan contracts with provisions that would allow schools to illegally withhold students academic transcripts or access to classes and other education services in the case of default. Some servicers also falsely threatened students with legal action. 
Federal loan servicers harming borrowers during return to repayment : CFPB supervision observed that federal loan servicers failed to provide, for extended time periods, adequate ways for borrowers to manage key loan issues by phone. Servicers also issued deceptive billing statements with incorrect payment amounts and due dates, and debited unauthorized amounts. Significantly, examiners also uncovered numerous problems with how servicers processed borrowers applications for income-driven repayment plans.
